In The Logic of Collective Action (1965), economist Mancur Olson challenged the popular idea that, in a democracy, the majority view will prevail, and in doing so launched the modern study of public economy, sometimes referred to as public choice, a subtopic of microeconomics. In this chapter, we will look at the economics of government policy, why smaller, more organized groups have an incentive to work hard to enact certain policies, and why lawmakers ultimately make decisions that may result in bad economic policy.

p9.original: Flaws in the Democratic System of Government
p9.zh: 政府民主制度中的缺陷

p10.original: As President Abraham Lincoln famously said in his 1863 Gettysburg Address, democratic governments are supposed to be “of the people, by the people, and for the people.” Can we rely on democratic governments to enact sensible economic policies? After all, they react to voters, not to analyses of demand and supply curves. The main focus of an economics course is, naturally enough, to analyze the characteristics of markets and purely economic institutions. However, political institutions also play a role in allocating society’s scarce resources, and economists have played an active role, along with other social scientists, in analyzing how such political institutions work.
p10.zh: 正如亚伯拉罕·林肯总统在1863年的格底斯堡讲话中著名的所说,民主政府应该是“人民、人民和人民 ” 。 我们可以依靠民主政府来制定明智的经济政策吗?毕竟,他们对选民作出反应,而不是对需求和供应曲线的分析作出反应。经济学课程的主要重点自然是分析市场和纯经济体制的特点。 然而,政治机构也在分配社会稀缺资源方面发挥作用,经济学家与其他社会科学家一起,在分析这种政治机构如何运作方面发挥了积极作用。

p11.original: Other chapters of this book discuss situations in which market forces can sometimes lead to undesirable results: monopoly, imperfect competition, and antitrust policy; negative and positive externalities; poverty and inequality of incomes; failures to provide insurance; and financial markets that may go from boom to bust. Many of these chapters suggest that the government's economic policies could address these issues.
p11.zh: 本书其他章节讨论了市场力量有时可能导致不良结果的情况:垄断、不完善的竞争和反托拉斯政策;消极和积极的外部性;贫穷和收入不平等;未能提供保险;以及金融市场可能从繁荣走向崩溃。其中许多章节建议政府的经济政策可以解决这些问题。

p12.original: However, just as markets can face issues and problems that lead to undesirable outcomes, a democratic system of government can also make mistakes, either by enacting policies that do not benefit society as a whole or by failing to enact policies that would have benefited society as a whole. This chapter discusses some practical difficulties of democracy from an economic point of view: we presume the actors in the political system follow their own self-interest, which is not necessarily the same as the public good. For example, many of those who are eligible to vote do not, which obviously raises questions about whether a democratic system will reflect everyone’s interests. Benefits or costs of government action are sometimes concentrated on small groups, which in some cases may organize and have a disproportionately large impact on politics and in other cases may fail to organize and end up neglected. A legislator who worries about support from voters in their district may focus on spending projects specific to the district without sufficient concern for whether this spending is in the nation's interest.
p12.zh: 然而,正如市场可能面临导致不良结果的问题和问题一样,民主政府制度也可能犯错误,要么颁布不利于整个社会的政策,要么未能颁布有利于整个社会的政策。本章从经济角度讨论了民主的一些实际困难:我们假定政治制度中的行为者遵循的是其自身的自身利益,这不一定等同于公益. 例如,许多有资格投票的人没有投票,这显然引起了民主制度是否将反映每个人的利益的问题。 政府行动的利益或成本有时集中在小团体上,在某些情况下,小团体可能组织起来,对政治产生不成比例的重大影响,而在另一些情况下,则可能无法组织和最终被忽视。立法者如果担心选区选民的支持,可以专注于支出该区特有的项目,而不必充分关注这一支出是否符合国家利益。

p13.original: When more than two choices exist, the principle that the majority of voters should decide may not always make logical sense, because situations can arise where it becomes literally impossible to decide what the “majority” prefers. Government may also be slower than private firms to correct its mistakes, because government agencies do not face competition or the threat of new entry.
p13.zh: 当存在两种以上选择时,多数选民决定的原则可能并不总是合乎逻辑的,因为当“多数”更喜欢什么就几乎不可能决定时,就会产生这种情况。 政府可能也比私营公司更慢地纠正其错误,因为政府机构没有面临竞争或新进入的威胁。

p14.original: Voter Participation and Costs of Elections

p15.original: In U.S. presidential elections over the last few decades, about 55% to 65% of voting-age citizens actually voted, according to the U.S. Census. In congressional elections when there is no presidential race, or in local elections, the turnout is typically lower, often less than half the eligible voters. In other countries, the share of adults who vote is often higher. For example, in national elections since the 1980s in Germany, Spain, and France, about 75% to 80% of those of voting age cast ballots. Even this total falls well short of 100%. Some countries have laws that require voting, among them Australia, Belgium, Italy, Greece, Turkey, Singapore, and most Latin American nations. At the time the United States was founded, voting was mandatory in Virginia, Maryland, Delaware, and Georgia. Even if the law can require people to vote, however, no law can require that each voter cast an informed or a thoughtful vote. Moreover, in the United States and in most countries around the world, the freedom to vote has also typically meant the freedom not to vote.
p15.zh: 在过去几十年的美国总统大选中,据美国统计,约55%到65%的投票年龄的公民实际投票.人口普查。 在没有总统选举的国会选举中,或地方选举中,投票率一般较低,往往不到合格选民的一半. 在其他国家,成年人投票的比例往往更高。 例如,自1980年代以来,在德国、西班牙和法国的全国选举中,投票年龄的选民约有75%至80%投了票。 即使这一总数也远远低于100%。有些国家有需要投票的法律,其中包括澳大利亚,比利时,意大利,希腊,土耳其,新加坡,以及大多数拉丁美洲国家. 美国成立时,投票在弗吉尼亚州,马里兰州,特拉华州和佐治亚州是强制性的. 然而,即使法律可以要求人民投票,但任何法律都不能要求每个选民进行知情或深思熟虑的投票。 此外,在美国和世界上大多数国家,投票自由也通常意味着不投票的自由。

p16.original: Why do people not vote? Perhaps they do not care too much about who wins, or they are uninformed about who is running, or they do not believe their vote will matter or change their lives in any way. These reasons are probably tied together, since people who do not believe their vote matters will not bother to become informed or care who wins. Economists have suggested why a utility-maximizing person might rationally decide not to vote or not to become informed about the election. While a single vote may decide a few elections in very small towns, in most elections of any size, the Board of Elections measures the margin of victory in hundreds, thousands, or even millions of votes. A rational voter will recognize that one vote is extremely unlikely to make a difference. This theory of rational ignorance holds that people will not vote if the costs of becoming informed and voting are too high, or they feel their vote will not be decisive in the election.
p16.zh: 为什么人们不投票? 也许他们并不过分关心谁赢了,或者他们不知道谁在竞选,或者他们不相信他们的投票会很重要,或者以任何方式改变他们的生活. 这些原因很可能是联系在一起的,因为不相信自己的投票问题的人将不费心去了解情况或关心谁赢了。经济学家们建议,为什么一个功用最大化的人可能理性地决定不投票或不了解选举情况。 虽然在非常小的城镇中,只有一票可以决定少数选举,但在大多数大小选举中,选举委员会以数百票、数千票甚至数百万票衡量胜利的幅度。 一个理性的选民会认识到,一票极不可能产生效果。 这种理性无知的理论认为,如果知情和投票的代价太高,或者他们觉得自己的投票不会在选举中起决定性作用,人们就不会投票.

p17.original: In a 1957 work, An Economic Theory of Democracy, the economist Anthony Downs stated the problem this way: “It seems probable that for a great many citizens in a democracy, rational behavior excludes any investment whatever in political information per se. No matter how significant a difference between parties is revealed to the rational citizen by his free information, or how uncertain he is about which party to support, he realizes that his vote has almost no chance of influencing the outcome… He will not even utilize all the free information available, since assimilating it takes time.” In his classic 1948 novel Walden Two, the psychologist B. F. Skinner puts the issue even more succinctly via one of his characters, who states: “The chance that one man’s vote will decide the issue in a national election…is less than the chance that he will be killed on his way to the polls.” The following Clear It Up feature explores another aspect of the election process: spending.

p18.original: How much is too much to spend on an election?

p19.original: In the 2020 elections, it is estimated that spending for president, Congress, and state and local offices amounted to $14.4 billion, more than twice what had been spent in 2016. The money raised went to the campaigns, including advertising, fundraising, travel, and staff. Many people worry that politicians spend too much time raising money and end up entangled with special interest groups that make major donations. Critics would prefer a system that restricts what candidates can spend, perhaps in exchange for limited public campaign financing or free television advertising time.
p19.zh: 在2020年的选举中,估计总统,国会以及州和地方办公室的支出达144亿美元,是2016年支出的两倍多.募集的资金用于竞选活动,包括广告、筹款、旅行和工作人员。许多人担心政客花太多时间筹集资金,最后与作出重大捐款的特殊利益集团纠缠在一起.批评者倾向于一种限制候选人开支的制度,或许可以换取有限的公共竞选资金或免费的电视广告时间。

p20.original: How much spending on campaigns is too much? Five billion dollars will buy many potato chips, but in the U.S. economy, which was nearly $21 trillion in 2020, the $14.4 billion spent on political campaigns was about 1/15th of 1% of the overall economy. Here is another way to think about campaign spending. Total government spending programs in 2020, including federal and state governments, was about $8.8 trillion, so the cost of choosing the people who would determine how to spend this money was less than 2/10 of 1% of that. In the context of the enormous U.S. economy, $14.4 billion is not as much money as it sounds. U.S. consumers spend almost $2 billion per year on toothpaste and $7 billion on hair care products. In 2020, Procter and Gamble spent almost $5 billion on advertising. It may seem peculiar that one company’s spending on advertisements amounts to one third of what is spent on presidential and other elections.
p20.zh: 竞选花费多少是太多?50亿美元将购买许多土豆薯片,但在2020年将近21万亿美元的美国经济中,用于政治竞选的144亿美元约占整个经济的1/15 %. 这里还有另一种思考竞选开支的方法.2020年政府总开支方案,包括联邦和州政府,大约为8.8万亿美元,因此选择决定如何使用这笔钱的人的成本不到1%的2/10。 在巨大的美国经济背景下,144亿美元并没有听起来那么多钱. 美国消费者每年在牙膏上花费近20亿美元,在美发护理产品上花费70亿美元.2020年,宝洁和甘布尔在广告上花费了近50亿美元.一家公司在广告方面的开支相当于总统选举和其他选举开支的三分之一,这似乎很奇怪。

p21.original: Whatever we believe about whether candidates and their parties spend too much or too little on elections, the U.S. Supreme Court has placed limits on how government can limit campaign spending. In a 1976 decision, Buckley v. Valeo, the Supreme Court emphasized that the First Amendment to the U.S. Constitution specifies freedom of speech. The federal government and states can offer candidates a voluntary deal in which government makes some public financing available to candidates, but only if the candidates agree to abide by certain spending limits. Of course, candidates can also voluntarily agree to set certain spending limits if they wish. However, government cannot forbid people or organizations to raise and spend money above these limits if they choose.
p21.zh: 不管我们相信什么 关于候选人和他们的政党 花费太多或太少用于选举, 美国。最高法院对政府如何限制竞选开支施加了限制。 在1976年的一项决定中,Buckley诉德国案Valeo),最高法院强调美国第一修正案. 《宪法》规定了言论自由。联邦政府和各州可以向候选人提供一项自愿协议,其中政府向候选人提供一些公共资金,但只有候选人同意遵守某些开支限制。 当然,如果候选人愿意,也可以自愿同意设定某些开支限额。 然而,政府不能禁止人民或组织在自己选择的情况下筹集和花费超过这些限额的资金.

p22.original: In 2002, Congress passed and President George W. Bush signed into law the Bipartisan Campaign Reform Act (BCRA). The relatively noncontroversial portions of the act strengthen the rules requiring full and speedy disclosure of who contributes money to campaigns. However, some controversial portions of the Act limit the ability of individuals and groups to make certain kinds of political donations and they ban certain kinds of advertising in the months leading up to an election. Some called these bans into question after the release of two films: Michael Moore’s Fahrenheit 9/11 and Citizens United’s Hillary: The Movie. At question was whether each film sought to discredit political candidates for office too close to an election, in violation of the BCRA. The lower courts found that Moore’s film did not violate the Act, while Citizens United’s did. The fight reached the Supreme Court, as Citizens United v. Federal Election Commission, saying that the First Amendment protects the rights of corporations as well as individuals to donate to political campaigns. The Court ruled, in a 5–4 decision, that the spending limits were unconstitutional. This controversial decision, which essentially allows unlimited contributions by corporations to political action committees, overruled several previous decisions and will likely be revisited in the future, due to the strength of the public reaction. For now, it has resulted in a sharp increase in election spending.
p22.zh: 2002年,国会通过,总统乔治·W.布什签署了《两党运动改革法》,使之成为法律。该法案中相对没有争议的部分加强了要求充分和迅速披露谁为竞选提供资金的规则。 然而,该法中一些有争议的部分限制了个人和团体提供某种政治捐助的能力,并且禁止在选举前的几个月内进行某些类型的广告宣传。 有些人在两部电影——迈克尔·摩尔的"华氏911"和"公民联合:电影"(Citizens ' United Hillary: The Movie)——上映后质疑这些禁令.问题是,每部电影是否试图破坏政治候选人的声誉,使其与选举过于接近,这违反了《布拉柴维尔宪法》。下级法院认定摩尔的电影没有违反该法,而公民联合公司则违反了该法。这场斗争已传到最高法院,因为公民联合诉最高法院案。联邦选举委员会说,第一修正案保护公司和个人向政治竞选活动捐款的权利。 法院在5-4项裁决中裁定,开支限额违宪。 这一有争议的决定基本上允许公司对政治行动委员会作出无限的贡献,推翻了先前的几项决定,由于公众反应的强烈性,今后可能再次作出这一决定。迄今,选举开支急剧增加。

p23.original: While many U.S. adults do not bother to vote in presidential elections, more than half do. What motivates them? Research on voting behavior has indicated that people who are more settled or more “connected” to society tend to vote more frequently. According to the Washington Post, more married people vote than single people. Those with a job vote more than the unemployed. Those who have lived longer in a neighborhood are more likely to vote than newcomers. Those who report that they know their neighbors and talk to them are more likely to vote than socially isolated people. Those with a higher income and level of education are also more likely to vote. These factors suggest that politicians are likely to focus more on the interests of married, employed, well-educated people with at least a middle-class level of income than on the interests of other groups. For example, those who vote may tend to be more supportive of financial assistance for the two-year and four-year colleges they expect their children to attend than they are of medical care or public school education aimed at families of unemployed people and those experiencing poverty.
p23.zh: 虽然许多美国成年人在总统选举中并不费心投票,但有一半以上的人会投票.是什么激励着他们?有关投票行为的研究表明,比较定居或与社会有“联系”的人往往更经常地投票。 根据"华盛顿邮报",已婚者投票比单身者多. 那些有工作票的人比失业的人还要多 那些在邻里居住时间较长的人比新来者更有可能投票. 那些报称认识邻居并与之交谈的人,比社会上孤立的人更有可能投票.收入和教育水平较高的人也更有可能投票。这些因素表明,政治家们可能更注重已婚、就业、受过良好教育、至少收入水平中等的人的利益,而不是其他群体的利益。 例如,投票者可能倾向于更支持两年制和四年制学院的财政援助,他们期望其子女上学,而不是接受针对失业者家庭和穷人的医疗保健或公立学校教育。

p24.zh: 访问这个网站,看看2020年不同团体的投票方式的细分.

p25.original: There have been many proposals to encourage greater voter turnout: making it easier to register to vote, keeping the polls open for more hours, or even moving Election Day to the weekend, when fewer people need to worry about jobs or school commitments. However, such changes do not seem to have caused a long-term upward trend in the number of people voting. After all, casting an informed vote will always impose some costs of time and energy. It is not clear how to strengthen people’s feeling of connectedness to society in a way that will lead to a substantial increase in voter turnout. Without greater voter turnout, however, politicians elected by the votes of 60% or fewer of the population may not enact economic policy in the best interests of 100% of the population. Meanwhile, countering a long trend toward making voting easier, many states have recently enacted new voting laws that critics say are actually barriers to voting. States have passed laws reducing early voting, restricting groups who are organizing get-out-the-vote efforts, enacted strict photo ID laws, as well as laws that require showing proof of U.S. citizenship. The ACLU argues that while these laws profess to prevent voter fraud, they are in effect making it harder for individuals to cast their vote.
p25.zh: 有许多建议鼓励提高选民投票率:让选民登记更加方便,让投票开放时间更长,甚至把选举日推到周末,因为那时需要担心工作或学校承诺的人更少. 然而,这些变化似乎并没有导致投票人数的长期上升趋势。毕竟,在知情的情况下投票总是会给时间和精力带来一些代价。 目前尚不清楚如何加强人们与社会的联系感,从而导致选民投票率的大幅提高。 然而,如果选民投票率不提高,由60%或更少的人口投票选出的政治家们可能无法制定符合100%人口最大利益的经济政策。 许多州最近颁布了新的投票法, 批评者认为这些法律实际上是投票的障碍。国家通过了减少提前投票的法律,限制组织投票的团体,颁布了严格的照片标识法,以及要求出示美国公民身份证明的法律。乌民盟认为,虽然这些法律宣称防止选民舞弊,但实际上使个人更难投票。

p27.original: The theory of rational ignorance says voters will recognize that their single vote is extremely unlikely to influence the outcome of an election. As a consequence, they will choose to remain uninformed about issues and not vote. This theory helps explain why voter turnout is so low in the United States.
p27.zh: 理性无知的理论说,选民会认识到他们的单一选票极不可能影响选举结果. 因此,他们将选择对问题保持不知情,而不是投票。 这一理论有助于解释为什么美国选民投票率如此低.

p29.original: Based on the theory of rational ignorance, what should we expect to happen to voter turnout as the internet makes information easier to obtain?
p29.zh: 根据理性无知的理论,当互联网使信息更容易获得时,我们期望选民投票率会怎样?

p30.original: All other things being equal, voter turnout should increase as the cost of casting an informed vote decreases.
p30.zh: 在所有其他情况相同的情况下,选民投票率应随着明智投票费用的减少而增加。

p31.original: What is the cost of voting in an election?
p31.zh: 在选举中投票的代价是多少?

p32.original: The cost in time of voting, transportation costs to and from the polling place, and any additional time and effort spent becoming informed about the candidates.

p49.original: Many political issues are of intense interest to a relatively small group, as we noted above. For example, many U.S. drivers do not much care where their car tires were made—they just want good quality as inexpensively as possible. In September 2009, President Obama and Congress enacted a tariff (taxes added on imported goods) on tires imported from China that would increase the price by 35 percent in its first year, 30 percent in its second year, and 25 percent in its third year. Interestingly, the U.S. companies that make tires did not favor this step, because most of them also import tires from China and other countries. (See Globalization and Protectionism for more on tariffs.) However, the United Steelworkers union, which had seen jobs in the tire industry fall by 5,000 over the previous five years, lobbied fiercely for the tariff. With this tariff, the cost of all tires increased significantly. (See the closing Bring It Home feature at the end of this chapter for more information on the tire tariff.)
p49.zh: 正如我们上文指出的,一个相对较小的集团对许多政治问题非常感兴趣。 例如,许多美国司机不太关心汽车轮胎的制造地点,他们只是尽可能地要求质量好。2009年9月,奥巴马总统和国会对从中国进口的轮胎制定了关税(进口商品税加征),该税加征价格将在第一年提高35%,第二年提高30%,第三年提高25%。有趣的是,制造轮胎的美国公司并不赞成这一步骤,因为大多数公司也从中国和其他国家进口轮胎. 然而,联合钢铁工人联盟在过去五年里减少了5 000个轮胎行业的工作,为关税进行了激烈的游说。有了这种关税,所有轮胎的成本都大大增加.(关于轮胎税的更多信息,请参见本章末尾的收尾带回家功能。 )

p50.original: Special interest groups are groups that are small in number relative to the nation, but quite well organized and focused on a specific issue. A special interest group can pressure legislators to enact public policies that do not benefit society as a whole. Imagine an environmental rule to reduce air pollution that will cost 10 large companies $8 million each, for a total cost of $80 million. The social benefits from enacting this rule provide an average benefit of $10 for every person in the United States; there are roughly 340 million people in the United States, for a total of about $3.4 billion. Even though the benefits are far higher than the costs for society as a whole, the 10 companies are likely to lobby much more fiercely to avoid $8 million in costs than the average person is to argue for $10 worth of benefits.
p50.zh: 特殊利益集团是相对于国家数量较少,但组织严密,重点针对特定问题的群体.特殊利益集团可以迫使立法者颁布不利于整个社会的公共政策。想象一下,减少空气污染的环境规则将花费10家大公司每人800万美元,总成本为8 000万美元。颁布这一规则的社会福利为美国每个人平均提供了10美元的福利;美国大约有3.4亿人,总计约34亿美元. 尽管收益远远高于整个社会的成本,但10家公司很可能比一般人主张价值10美元的收益要激烈得多地游说,以避免800万美元的费用。

p51.original: As this example suggests, we can relate the problem of special interests in politics to an issue we raised in Environmental Protection and Negative Externalities about economic policy with respect to negative externalities and pollution—the problem called regulatory capture (which we defined in Monopoly and Antitrust Policy). In legislative bodies and agencies that write laws and regulations about how much corporations will pay in taxes, or rules for safety in the workplace, or instructions on how to satisfy environmental regulations, you can be sure the specific industry affected has lobbyists who study every word and every comma. They talk with the legislators who are writing the legislation and suggest alternative wording. They contribute to the campaigns of legislators on the key committees—and may even offer those legislators high-paying jobs after they have left office. As a result, it often turns out that those regulated can exercise considerable influence over the regulators.
p51.zh: 正如这个例子所表明的那样,我们可以将政治上的特殊利益问题与我们在环境保护和消极的外在因素中提出的一个问题联系起来,即关于消极的外在因素和污染的经济政策问题,即所谓的管制捕捉问题(我们在垄断和反托拉斯政策中对此作了界定)。 在那些制定公司将缴纳多少税、工作场所安全规则或如何遵守环境条例的指示的立法机关和机构中,你可以肯定受影响的具体行业有游说者,他们研究每一个字和每一个逗号。 他们与正在起草立法的立法者交谈,并提出备选措辞。 他们为立法者在关键委员会上的活动作出贡献——甚至可以在这些立法者卸任后为他们提供高薪工作。 因此,往往发现这些受监管的机构可对监管机构施加相当大的影响。

p52.original: Visit this website to read about lobbying.
p52.zh: 访问此网站阅读游说内容.

p53.original: In the early 2000s, about 40 million people in the United States were eligible for Medicare, a government program that provides health insurance for those 65 and older. On some issues, the elderly are a powerful interest group. They donate money and time to political campaigns, and in the 2020 presidential election, 76% of those ages 65–74 voted, while just 51% of those aged 18 to 24 cast a ballot, according to the U.S. Census.
p53.zh: 2000年代初,美国约有4 000万人有资格享受医疗保险,这是为65岁及以上者提供医疗保险的政府方案。在一些问题上,老年人是一个强大的利益群体。 他们为政治竞选献出金钱和时间,在2020年的总统选举中,65至74岁年龄段的76%的人投票,而根据美国的说法,18至24岁年龄段的人中只有51%投了选票。人口普查。

p54.original: In 2003, Congress passed and President George Bush signed into law a substantial expansion of Medicare that helped the elderly to pay for prescription drugs. The prescription drug benefit cost the federal government about $40 billion in 2006, and the Medicare system projected that the annual cost would rise to $121 billion by 2016. The political pressure to pass a prescription drug benefit for Medicare was apparently quite high, while the political pressure to assist the 40 million with no health insurance at all was considerably lower. One reason might be that the American Association for Retired People AARP, a well-funded and well-organized lobbying group represents senior citizens, while there is no umbrella organization to lobby for those without health insurance.
p54.zh: 2003年,国会通过,乔治·布什总统签署了大幅扩大医疗保健计划的法律,帮助老年人支付处方药费用。2006年处方药福利使联邦政府花费了约400亿美元,而医疗保险体系预计到2016年,年度成本将上升到1,210亿美元.要求为医疗保险提供处方药品福利的政治压力显然相当大,而要求帮助4 000万没有医疗保险的政治压力则大大降低。 一个原因可能是美国退休者协会是一个资金充足和组织良好的游说团体,代表老年公民,而没有伞式组织为那些没有医疗保险的人进行游说。

p55.original: In the battle over passage of the 2010 Affordable Care Act (ACA), which became known as “Obamacare,” there was heavy lobbying on all sides by insurance companies and pharmaceutical companies. However, labor unions and community groups financed a lobby group, Health Care for America Now (HCAN), to offset corporate lobbying. HCAN, spending $60 million dollars, was successful in helping pass legislation which added new regulations on insurance companies and a mandate that all individuals will obtain health insurance by 2014. The following Work It Out feature further explains voter incentives and lobbyist influence.
p55.zh: 在为2010年《负担得起的护理法》(ACA)的通过而展开的战斗中,该法被称为“奥巴马护理”,保险公司和制药公司在各方进行了激烈的游说。 然而,工会和社区团体资助了一个游说团体,即 " 立即美国保健 " (HCAN),以抵消企业游说。HCAN耗资6000万美元,成功帮助通过立法,增加了关于保险公司的新条例,并授权所有人到2014年获得健康保险。 下面的《工作外传》进一步解释了选民奖励和游说的影响。

p57.original: Suppose Congress proposes a tax on carbon emissions for certain factories in a small town of 10,000 people. Congress estimates the tax will reduce pollution to such an extent that it will benefit each resident by an equivalent of $300. The tax will also reduce profits to the town’s two large factories by $1 million each. How much should the factory owners be willing to spend to fight the tax passage, and how much should the townspeople be willing to pay to support it? Why is society unlikely to achieve the optimal outcome?
p57.zh: 假设国会建议对一万人口的小镇的某些工厂征收碳排放税.国会估计,这种税将减少污染,使每个居民得到相当于300美元的惠益。税收也会减少城镇两家大型工厂的利润,每家将减少100万美元.工厂主应愿意花多少钱来抗衡税过关,镇民应愿意花多少钱来支撑它? 为什么社会不可能取得最佳结果?

p58.original: Step 1. The two factory owners each stand to lose $1 million if the tax passes, so each should be willing to spend up to that amount to prevent the passage, a combined sum of $2 million. Of course, in the real world, there is no guarantee that lobbying efforts will be successful, so the factory owners may choose to invest an amount that is substantially lower.
p58.zh: 步骤1。 如果税额过户,两个工厂的业主每人将损失100万美元,因此,每人应愿意花费最高的金额防止通过,合计200万美元。 当然,在现实世界里,游说努力是不能保证成功的,所以工厂业主可以选择投资数额大大降低.

p59.original: Step 2. There are 10,000 townspeople, each standing to benefit by $300 if the tax passes. Theoretically, then, they should be willing to spend up to $3 million (10,000 × $300) to ensure passage. (Again, in the real world with no guarantees of success, they may choose to spend less.)
p59.zh: 步骤二.城镇居民有10,000人,如果税收过关,每人可领取300美元。 从理论上讲,他们应该愿意花费高达300万美元(10,000×300美元),以确保通过.(又曰,在现实世界中,虽无成功之保证,可选少费. )

p60.original: Step 3. It is costly and difficult for 10,000 people to coordinate in such a way as to influence public policy. Since each person stands to gain only $300, many may feel lobbying is not worth the effort.
p60.zh: 步骤3。 对10 000人来说,以影响公共政策的方式进行协调是代价高昂和困难的。 由于每人只得300美元,许多人可能觉得游说并不值得。

p61.original: Step 4. The two factory owners, however, find it very easy and profitable to coordinate their activities, so they have a greater incentive to do so.
p61.zh: 步骤4。 然而,两个工厂的业主发现协调他们的活动非常容易和有利可图,因此他们有更大的动力来这样做.

p62.original: Special interests may develop a close relationship with one political party, so their ability to influence legislation rises and falls as that party moves in or out of power. A special interest may even hurt a political party if it appears to a number of voters that the relationship is too cozy. In a close election, a small group that has been under-represented in the past may find that it can tip the election one way or another—so that group will suddenly receive considerable attention. Democratic institutions produce an ebb and flow of political parties and interests and thus offer both opportunities for special interests and ways of counterbalancing those interests over time.
p62.zh: 特殊利益可能与一个政党发展密切关系,因此随着该政党上台或下台,他们影响立法的能力会上升或下降. 如果一些选民认为关系过于舒适,那么特别的兴趣甚至会伤害政党。 在一次临近的选举中,一个过去代表性不足的小组可能会发现,它可以以这样或那样的方式向选举倾斜,因此这个小组会突然受到相当的关注.民主机构产生政党和利益流,从而既为特殊利益提供机会,也为长期平衡这些利益提供了途径。

p63.zh: 可识别的赢家,匿名输家

p64.original: A number of economic policies produce gains whose beneficiaries are easily identifiable, but costs that are partly or entirely shared by a large number who remain anonymous. A democratic political system probably has a bias toward those who are identifiable.
p64.zh: 一些经济政策产生收益,受益者很容易确定,但成本部分或完全由许多匿名者分担。民主政治制度可能偏向那些可以识别的人。

p65.original: For example, policies that impose price controls—like rent control—may look as if they benefit renters and impose costs only on landlords. However, when landlords then decide to reduce the number of rental units available in the area, a number of people who would have liked to rent an apartment end up living somewhere else because no units were available. These would-be renters have experienced a cost of rent control, but it is hard to identify who they are.
p65.zh: 例如,实行价格控制的政策——类似租金控制——可能看起来像对租户有利,只给房东带来费用。 然而,当房东随后决定减少该地区现有的租房单位数量时,一些本来想租房的人最终会因为没有租房单位而住在别的地方. 这些将要租房的人经历了租金控制的费用,但很难确定他们是谁。

p66.original: Similarly, policies that block imports will benefit the firms that would have competed with those imports—and workers at those firms—who are likely to be quite visible. Consumers who would have preferred to purchase the imported products, and who thus bear some costs of the protectionist policy, are much less visible.
p66.zh: 同样,阻止进口的政策将有利于本来会与这些进口竞争的公司——以及这些公司的工人——他们很可能相当明显。消费者本来更愿意购买进口产品,因此承担保护主义政策的一些费用,但这种人却更不引人注目。

p67.original: Specific tax breaks and spending programs also have identifiable winners and impose costs on others who are hard to identify. Special interests are more likely to arise from a group that is easily identifiable, rather than from a group where some of those who suffer may not even recognize they are bearing costs.
p67.zh: 具体的减税和支出方案也有可识别的赢家,并给难以识别的其他人带来成本。特殊利益更有可能来自易于识别的集团,而不是来自某些受难者可能甚至不承认自己承担费用的集团。

p69.original: Politicians have an incentive to ensure that they spend government money in their home state or district, where it will benefit their constituents in a direct and obvious way. Thus, when legislators are negotiating over whether to support a piece of legislation, they commonly ask each other to include pork-barrel spending, legislation that benefits mainly a single political district. Pork-barrel spending is another case in which concentrated benefits and widely dispersed costs challenge democracy: the benefits of pork-barrel spending are obvious and direct to local voters, while the costs are spread over the entire country. Read the following Clear It Up feature for more information on pork-barrel spending.
p69.zh: 政治家们有动力确保他们把政府的钱花在自己的国家或地区,在那里,政府资金将直接和明显地为选民带来好处。 因此,当立法者正在就是否支持一项立法进行谈判时,他们通常要求彼此包括猪肉桶支出,这种立法主要有利于单一的政治区。猪桶式支出是集中收益和广泛分散的成本挑战民主的又一案例:猪桶式支出的效益是显而易见的,并且直接针对当地选民,而成本则分散于全国.有关猪肉桶支出的更多信息,请查看以下 Clear It Up 功能。

p70.original: How much impact can pork-barrel spending have?
p70.zh: 猪肉桶花能产生多大影响?.

p71.original: Many observers widely regard U.S. Senator Robert C. Byrd of West Virginia, who was originally elected to the Senate in 1958 and served until 2010, as one of the masters of pork-barrel politics, directing a steady stream of federal funds to his home state. A journalist once compiled a list of structures in West Virginia at least partly government funded and named after Byrd: “the Robert C. Byrd Highway; the Robert C. Byrd Locks and Dam; the Robert C. Byrd Institute; the Robert C. Byrd Life Long Learning Center; the Robert C. Byrd Honors Scholarship Program; the Robert C. Byrd Green Bank Telescope; the Robert C. Byrd Institute for Advanced Flexible Manufacturing; the Robert C. Byrd Federal Courthouse; the Robert C. Byrd Health Sciences Center; the Robert C. Byrd Academic and Technology Center; the Robert C. Byrd United Technical Center; the Robert C. Byrd Federal Building; the Robert C. Byrd Drive; the Robert C. Byrd Hilltop Office Complex; the Robert C. Byrd Library; and the Robert C. Byrd Learning Resource Center; the Robert C. Byrd Rural Health Center.” This list does not include government-funded projects in West Virginia that were not named after Byrd. Of course, we would have to analyze each of these expenditures in detail to figure out whether we should treat them as pork-barrel spending or whether they provide widespread benefits that reach beyond West Virginia. At least some of them, or a portion of them, certainly would fall into that category. Because there are currently no term limits for Congressional representatives, those who have been in office longer generally have more power to enact pork-barrel projects.
p71.zh: 许多观察者广泛认为美国.参议员罗伯特·C. 西弗吉尼亚州伯德最初于1958年当选参议院议员,并担任猪缸政治的大师之一直至2010年,他指挥着稳定流的联邦资金前往他的家乡州. 一位记者曾编集过一份西弗吉尼亚州的结构列表,至少部分由政府资助,并以伯德的名字命名:"The Robert C.伯德高速公路; 罗伯特 C.伯德洛克斯和达姆; 罗伯特 C.伯德研究所; 罗伯特·C.Byrd终身学习中心; Robert C.伯德荣誉奖学金计划; 罗伯特·C.伯德·格林银行望远镜; 罗伯特C.伯德高级弹性制造研究所; Robert C.伯德联邦法院; 罗伯特 C.Byrd健康科学中心; Robert C.伯德学术和技术中心; 罗伯特·C.伯德联合技术中心; 罗伯特C.伯德联邦大厦; 罗伯特C.伯德车道; 罗伯特C.Byrd Hilltop Office Complex; 罗伯特C.伯德图书馆;和罗伯特·C.Byrd学习资源中心; Robert C.Byrd农村保健中心。” 本列表不包括西弗吉尼亚州政府资助的、没有以Byrd命名的项目。 当然,我们必须详细分析这些开支的每一项,以确定我们是否应该把它们当作猪肉桶的开支,或者它们是否提供了超越西弗吉尼亚州的广泛利益. 至少其中一些,或其中的一部分,肯定属于这一类别。 由于目前国会代表没有任期限制,那些在任时间较长的议员一般拥有更大的权力来实施猪肉桶项目.

p72.original: The amount that government spends on individual pork-barrel projects is small, but many small projects can add up to a substantial total. A nonprofit watchdog organization, called Citizens against Government Waste, produces an annual report, the Pig Book that attempts to quantify the amount of pork-barrel spending, focusing on items that only one member of Congress requested, that were passed into law without any public hearings, or that serve only a local purpose. Whether any specific item qualifies as pork can be controversial. The 2021 Congressional Pig Book identified 285 earmarks in FY 2021, with a cost of $16.8 billion. Recent growth in earmarks and their cost is apparent: in FY 2017, there were 163 earmarks at a cost of $6.8 billion. Hence, in only four years, there was a 75% increase in the number of earmarks and a 147% increase in the cost of those earmarks.
p72.zh: 政府花在个人猪肉桶项目上的数额很小,但许多小项目的总和可相当大。 一个名为“公民反对政府废物”的非营利监督组织每年编制一份报告,即《猪皮书》,试图量化猪肉桶的支出额,重点放在只有一名国会议员提出要求、未经任何公开听证就被通过为法律或只服务于地方目的的项目上。任何特定物品是否有资格成为猪肉,都会引起争议.2021国会猪皮书在2021财政年度确定了285项专项拨款,费用为168亿美元. 最近指定用途款项的增长及其费用是显而易见的:2017财政年度,有163项指定用途款项,费用为68亿美元。 因此,仅在四年内,指定用途的数量就增加了75%,这些指定用途的成本就增加了147%。

p73.original: Logrolling, an action in which all members of a group of legislators agree to vote for a package of otherwise unrelated laws that they individually favor, can encourage pork barrel spending. For example, if one member of the U.S. Congress suggests building a new bridge or hospital in their own congressional district, the other members might oppose it. However, if 51% of the legislators come together, they can pass a bill that includes a bridge or hospital for every one of their districts.
p73.zh: 伐木是一组立法者所有成员都同意投票支持他们各自赞成的一揽子不相关的法律的一项行动,它可以鼓励猪肉桶消费。 例如,如果一个美国成员.国会建议在他们自己的国会区建造一座新桥或医院,其他成员可能反对. 但是,如果51%的立法者聚集在一起,他们可以通过一项法案,包括为其每个地区建造一座桥梁或医院。

p74.original: As a reflection of this interest of legislators in their own districts, the U.S. government has typically spread out its spending on military bases and weapons programs to congressional districts all across the country. In part, the government does this to help create a situation that encourages members of Congress to vote in support of defense spending.
p74.zh: 美国政府通常将军事基地和武器方案的开支分散到全国各地的国会区,这反映了立法者对本选区的这种兴趣。部分地,政府这样做是为了帮助造成一种鼓励国会议员投票支持国防开支的局面.

p76.original: Special interest politics arises when a relatively small group, called a special interest group, each of whose members has a large interest in a political outcome, devotes considerable time and energy to lobbying for the group’s preferred choice. Meanwhile, the large majority, each of whose members has only a small interest in this issue, pays no attention.
p76.zh: 当一个相对较小的团体,称为一个特别利益团体,每个成员对政治结果都有很大的兴趣时,就会产生特别利益政治,他们花大量时间和精力游说该团体的首选。 与此同时,大多数成员对这个问题兴趣不大,他们都不注意。

p77.original: We define pork--barrel spending as legislation whose benefits are concentrated on a single district while the costs are spread widely over the country. Logrolling refers to a situation in which two or more legislators agree to vote for each other’s legislation, which can then encourage pork-barrel spending in many districts.
p77.zh: 我们把猪肉桶开支定义为立法,其收益集中在一个地区,而费用则在全国广泛分配。伐木是指两个或两个以上立法者同意投票支持对方立法的情况,这样可以鼓励许多地区的猪肉桶开支.

p79.original: What is the main factor preventing a large community from influencing policy in the same way as a special interest group?
p79.zh: 是什么主要因素妨碍一个大社区以与特殊利益集团相同的方式影响政策?

p80.original: The costs of organization and the small benefit to the individual.
p80.zh: 组织成本和对个人的小额利益。

p81.original: Why might legislators vote to impose a tariff on Egyptian cotton, when consumers in their districts would benefit from its availability?
p81.zh: 为什么立法者会投票对埃及的棉花征收关税,而他们地区的消费者将受益于其供应?

p82.original: Domestic cotton producers would lobby heavily to protect themselves from the competition, whereas the consumers have little incentive to organize.
p82.zh: 国内棉花生产者将大力游说,保护自己免受竞争的影响,而消费者组织起来的动力却很少。

p84.original: How can a small special interest group win in a situation of majority voting when the benefits it seeks flow only to a small group?
p84.zh: 在多数投票的情况下,一个小的特殊利益集团如果只追求一个小集团的利益,怎么能赢得呢?

p85.original: How can pork-barrel spending occur in a situation of majority voting when it benefits only a small group?
p85.zh: 在多数投票的情况下,如果猪肉桶的支出只惠及一个小群体,那么这种支出如何发生?

p86.original: Why do legislators vote for spending projects in districts that are not their own?
p86.zh: 为什么立法者会投票决定非本区的支出项目?

p88.original: When Microsoft was founded, the company devoted very few resources to lobbying activities. After a high-profile antitrust case against it, however, the company began to lobby heavily. Why does it make financial sense for companies to invest in lobbyists?
p88.zh: 微软成立后,公司投入很少的资源进行游说活动. 然而,公司在面对一个引人注目的反托拉斯案之后,开始大力游说. 为什么公司投资游说者在经济上是有意义的?

p89.original: Representatives of competing firms often comprise special interest groups. Why are competitors sometimes willing to cooperate in order to form lobbying associations?
p89.zh: 竞争公司的代表往往包括特殊利益集团。 为什么竞争者有时愿意合作组建游说协会?

p90.original: Special interests do not oppose regulations in all cases. The Marketplace Fairness Act of 2013 would require online merchants to collect sales taxes from their customers in other states. Why might a large online retailer like Amazon.com support such a measure?
p90.zh: 特殊利益并不反对所有情况下的条例。2013年《市场公平法》要求网上商家向其他国家的客户征收销售税。 为什么像Amazon.com这样的大型在线零售商会支持这样的措施?

p91.original: To ensure safety and efficacy, the Food and Drug Administration regulates the medicines that pharmacies are allowed to sell in the United States. Sometimes this means a company must test a drug for years before it can reach the market. We can easily identify the winners in this system as those who are protected from unsafe drugs that might otherwise harm them. Who are the more anonymous losers who do not benefit from strict medical regulations?
p91.zh: 为确保安全性和有效性,食品药品管理局对美国允许药店销售的药品进行监管. 有时这意味着公司必须测试药物多年才能进入市场. 我们可以很容易地将这一系统中的获胜者确定为那些受到保护,免受否则可能伤害他们的不安全药物之害的人。谁是没有从严格的医疗条例中受益的更匿名的失败者?

p92.original: How is it possible to bear a cost without realizing it? What are some examples of policies that affect people in ways of which they may not even be aware?
p92.zh: 不意识到就承担费用是不可能做到的?有哪些政策以他们甚至不知道的方式影响人民?

p93.original: Is pork-barrel spending always a bad thing? Can you think of some examples of pork-barrel projects, perhaps from your own district, that have had positive results?
p93.zh: 猪肉桶花总是坏事吗? 你能否想到一些猪肉桶项目的例子,也许来自你所在的区,已经取得了积极的成果?

p95.original: Say that the government is considering a ban on smoking in restaurants in Tobaccoville. There are 1 million people living there, and each would benefit by $200 from this smoking ban. However, there are two large tobacco companies in Tobaccoville and the ban would cost them $5 million each. What are the proposed policy's total costs and benefits? Do you think it will pass?
p95.zh: 说政府正在考虑禁止烟草镇餐馆吸烟.当地有100万人,每人从这项禁烟措施中受益200美元。 然而,烟草镇有两家大型烟草公司,禁烟将耗资500万美元。 拟议政策的总成本和效益是什么? 你觉得会过去吗?

p97.original: Roper Center Public Opinion Archives. “A Brief History of Public Opinion on the Government’s Role in Providing Health Care.” Last modified September 23, 2013.
p97.zh: 罗珀中心舆论档案馆. 《关于政府在提供保健方面的作用的民意概要》,2013年9月23日最后一次修订。

p98.original: U.S. Department of Commerce: United States Census Bureau. “Voting and Registration: Historical Time Series Tables; Table A-10: Reported Registration Rates in Presidential Election Years, by Selected Characteristics: November 1968 to 2012.” http://www.census.gov/hhes/www/socdemo/voting/publications/historical/index.html
p98.zh: 美国.商务部: 美国人口调查局.“投票和登记:历史时间序列表;表A-10:1968年11月至2012年按选定特征分列的总统选举年份报告登记率”。 http://www.census.gov/hhes/www/socdemo/voting/publications/historical/index.html

p99.original: Flaws in the Democratic System of Government
p99.zh: 政府民主制度中的缺陷

p100.original: Most developed countries today have a democratic system of government: citizens express their opinions through votes and those votes affect the direction of the country. The advantage of democracy over other systems is that it allows everyone in a society an equal say and therefore may reduce the possibility of a small group of wealthy oligarchs oppressing the masses. There is no such thing as a perfect system, and democracy, for all its popularity, is not without its problems, a few of which we will examine here.
p100.zh: 今天大多数发达国家都有一个民主的政府制度:公民通过选票表达自己的意见,这些选票会影响国家的方向.民主相对于其他制度的优势在于它让社会中的每一个人有平等的发言权,从而可能减少一小撮富裕的寡头压迫群众的可能性.不存在一个完美的制度,民主,就其所有受欢迎的事物而言,并非没有它的问题,我们在这里将审查其中的几个问题。

p101.original: We sometimes sum up and oversimplify democracy in two words: “Majority rule.” When voters face three or more choices, however, then voting may not always be a useful way of determining what the majority prefers.
p101.zh: 我们有时会用两个词来概括和过度简化民主:“多数人统治 ” 。 但是,当选民面临三种或三种以上选择时,投票可能并不总是决定多数人喜欢什么的有用方式。

p102.original: As one example, consider an election in a state where 60% of the population is liberal and 40% is conservative. If there are only two candidates, one from each side, and if liberals and conservatives vote in the same 60–40 proportions in which they are represented in the population, then the liberal will win. What if the election ends up including two liberal candidates and one conservative? It is possible that the liberal vote will split and victory will go to the minority party. In this case, the outcome does not reflect the majority’s preference.
p102.zh: 例如,在60%的人口是自由派的,40%是保守派的州,考虑选举。 如果只有两名候选人,双方各一名,如果自由派和保守派以他们在人口中代表的60–40的比例投票,那么自由派就会获胜. 如果选举最终包括两名自由党候选人和一名保守党人呢?有可能自由派的投票会分裂,胜利会归于少数党. 在这种情况下,结果并不反映多数人的偏好。

p103.original: Does the majority view prevail in the case of sugar quotas? Clearly there are more sugar consumers in the United States than sugar producers, but the U.S. domestic sugar lobby (www.sugarcane.org) has successfully argued for protection against imports since 1789. By law, therefore, U.S. cookie and candy makers must use 85% domestic sugar in their products. Meanwhile quotas on imported sugar restrict supply and keep the domestic sugar price up—raising prices for companies that use sugar in producing their goods and for consumers. The European Union allows sugar imports, and prices there are 40% lower than U.S. sugar prices. Sugar-producing countries in the Caribbean repeatedly protest the U.S. quotas at the World Trade Organization meetings, but each bite of cookie, at present, costs you more than if there were no sugar lobby. This case goes against the theory of the “median” voter in a democracy. The median voter theory argues that politicians will try to match policies to what pleases the median voter preferences. If we think of political positions along a spectrum from left to right, the median voter is in the middle of the spectrum. This theory argues that actual policy will reflect “middle of the road.” In the case of sugar lobby politics, the minority, not the median, dominates policy.
p103.zh: 在糖配额方面,多数人的看法是否占上风? 显然,美国食糖的消费者比糖生产商多,但美国国内食糖游说团(www.sugarcane.org)自1789年以来成功地提出了防止进口的保护措施。 因此,根据法律,美国饼干和糖果制造商必须在其产品中使用85%的家用糖. 与此同时,进口糖的配额限制供应,使国内糖价不断上涨,使生产商品时使用糖的公司和消费者的糖价不断上涨。 欧盟允许糖料进口,价格比美国糖料价格低40%.加勒比海的糖生产国在世界贸易组织会议上一再抗议美国的配额,但目前每咬一块饼干,比没有糖游说团要花费你更多的钱. 这一案件违背了民主国家“中间”选民的理论。中位选民理论认为,政治家们会试图将政策与中位选民偏好相匹配。 如果我们想一想从左到右的政治立场,中位选民就处于该频谱的中间。 这一理论认为,实际政策将反映“中途 ” 。 就糖游说政治而言,少数而不是中位数主导政策。

p104.original: Sometimes it is not even clear how to define the majority opinion. Step aside from politics for a moment and think about a choice facing three families (the Ortegas, the Schmidts, and the Alexanders) who are planning to celebrate New Year’s Day together. They agree to vote on the menu, choosing from three entrees, and they agree that the majority vote wins. With three families, it seems reasonable that one producing choice will get a 2–1 majority. What if, however, their vote ends up looking like ?
p104.zh: 有时甚至不清楚如何界定多数人的意见。与政治隔开一阵子, 想想面对三个家庭(奥特加斯家族、施密特家族和亚历山大家族)的抉择, 他们同意在菜单上投票,从三个主菜中选择,他们同意多数票获胜.有三个家庭,一个生产选择会获得2比1的多数,这似乎是合理的。 但是,如果,他们的投票结果 看起来像?

p105.original: Clearly, the three families disagree on their first choice. However, the problem goes even deeper. Instead of looking at all three choices at once, compare them two at a time. (See ) In a vote of turkey versus beef, turkey wins by 2–1. In a vote of beef versus lasagna, beef wins 2–1. If turkey beats beef, and beef beats lasagna, then it might seem only logical that turkey must also beat lasagna. However, with the preferences, lasagna is preferred to turkey by a 2–1 vote, as well. If lasagna is preferred to turkey, and turkey beats beef, then surely it must be that lasagna also beats beef? Actually, no. Beef beats lasagna. In other words, the majority view may not win. Clearly, as any car salesperson will tell you, the way one presents choices to us influences our decisions.
p105.zh: 显然,这三个家庭在第一选择上意见不一。 然而,问题更为严重。与其同时审视所有三种选择,不如一次比较两种选择.(参见)火鸡对牛肉的投票中,火鸡以2比1获胜. 在牛肉对面条的投票中,牛肉获胜2比1. 如果火鸡比牛肉,牛肉比面条,那么火鸡也得比面条,这似乎只是合乎逻辑的. 不过,由于偏好,千层面饼也以2–1票的比火鸡好. 如果面条比火鸡更受欢迎,而火鸡比牛肉还强,那肯定就是面条也比牛肉强吧? 其实没有。牛肉会打千层面条换句话说,多数观点可能不会获胜。 显然,任何汽车推销员都会告诉你, 给我们带来选择的方式会影响我们的决定。

p124.original: We call the situation in which Choice A is preferred by a majority over Choice B, Choice B is preferred by a majority over Choice C, and Choice C is preferred by a majority over Choice A a voting cycle. It is easy to imagine sets of government choices—say, perhaps the choice between increased defense spending, increased government spending on health care, and a tax cut—in which a voting cycle could occur. The result will be determined by the order in which interested parties present and vote on choices, not by majority rule, because every choice is both preferred to some alternative and also not preferred to another alternative.
p124.zh: 我们把选择A比选择B更受青睐的情况称为选择A,选择B比选择C更受青睐,选择C比选择A更受青睐的情况称为表决周期。很容易想象政府的选择,比如说,在增加国防开支、增加政府在保健方面的开支和削减税收之间作出选择,从而可以实行投票周期。其结果将由有关当事方就选择提出并进行表决的顺序决定,而不是多数规则,因为每一种选择都比某种选择更可取,也并非也比另一种选择更好。

p125.original: Visit this website to read about ranked choice voting, a preferential voting system.
p125.zh: 访问这个网站阅读有关排名选择投票,一种优先投票制度.

p126.zh: 政府自我更正机制在哪里?

p127.original: When a firm produces a product no one wants to buy or produces at a higher cost than its competitors, the firm is likely to suffer losses. If it cannot change its ways, it will go out of business. This self-correcting mechanism in the marketplace can have harsh effects on workers or on local economies, but it also puts pressure on firms for good performance.
p127.zh: 如果一家公司生产的产品无人愿意以比其竞争者更高的成本购买或生产,公司就有可能遭受损失。 如果它不能改变它的方式,它就会失去业务。 这种市场中的自我纠正机制可能对工人或当地经济产生严重影响,但也对公司造成良好业绩的压力。

p128.original: Government agencies, however, do not sell their products in a market. They receive tax dollars instead. They are not challenged by competitors as are private-sector firms. If the U.S. Department of Education or the U.S. Department of Defense is performing poorly, citizens cannot purchase their services from another provider and drive the existing government agencies into bankruptcy. If you are upset that the Internal Revenue Service is slow in sending you a tax refund or seems unable to answer your questions, you cannot decide to pay your income taxes through a different organization. Of course, elected politicians can assign new leaders to government agencies and instruct them to reorganize or to emphasize a different mission. The pressure government faces, however, to change its bureaucracy, to seek greater efficiency, and to improve customer responsiveness is much milder than the threat of being put out of business altogether.
p128.zh: 然而,政府机构不在其市场销售产品。 他们得到的税收美元代替。竞争者不象私营部门公司那样对竞争者提出质疑。 如是诸国.教育部或美国.国防部表现不佳,公民不能从另一供应商购买服务,并迫使现有政府机构破产。国内税务局不快地给你发退税,或似乎无法回答你的问题,所以不能决定通过不同的组织缴纳所得税。 当然,当选的政治家可以指派新的领导人到政府机构,并指示他们重组或强调不同的使命。 然而,政府面临的压力是改变其官僚机构,寻求更高的效率,提高客户的反应能力,这比被完全取缔经营的威胁要温和得多。

p129.original: This insight suggests that when government provides goods or services directly, we might expect it to do so with less efficiency than private firms—except in certain cases where the government agency may compete directly with private firms. At the local level, for example, government can provide directly services like garbage collection, using private firms under contract to the government, or by a mix of government employees competing with private firms.
p129.zh: 这种见解表明,当政府直接提供商品或服务时,我们可能期望政府这样做的效率低于私营公司,除非在某些情况下政府机构可能直接与私营公司竞争。 例如,在地方一级,政府可以直接提供垃圾收集等服务,利用与政府签订合同的私营公司,或由政府雇员与私营公司竞争。

p130.original: A Balanced View of Markets and Government
p130.zh: 市场和政府的平衡观点

p131.original: The British statesman Sir Winston Churchill (1874–1965) once wrote: “No one pretends that democracy is perfect or all-wise. Indeed, it has been said that democracy is the worst form of government except for all of the other forms which have been tried from time to time.” In that spirit, the theme of this discussion is certainly not that we should abandon democratic government. A practical student of public policy needs to recognize that in some cases, like the case of well-organized special interests or pork-barrel legislation, a democratic government may seek to enact economically unwise projects or programs. In other cases, by placing a low priority on the problems of those who are not well organized or who are less likely to vote, the government may fail to act when it could do some good. In these and other cases, there is no automatic reason to believe that government will necessarily make economically sensible choices.
p131.zh: 英国政治家温斯顿·丘吉尔爵士(1874年–1965年)曾写道:"没有人假装民主是完美的或全智的. 的确,有人说,民主是政府的最恶劣形式,除了不时尝试的所有其他形式外。” 本着这种精神,本次讨论的主题当然不是我们应该放弃民主政府。公共政策的实践学生需要认识到,在某些情况下,如组织良好的特殊利益或猪笼草立法,民主政府可能寻求制定经济上不明智的项目或方案。 在其他情况下,由于对组织不完善或投票可能性较小的人的问题不重视,政府可能在其能产生一定效果时不采取行动. 在这类和其他情况下,没有自动的理由相信政府必然作出经济上合理的选择。

p132.original: “The true test of a first-rate mind is the ability to hold two contradictory ideas at the same time,” wrote the American author F. Scott Fitzgerald (1896–1940). At this point in your study of microeconomics, you should be able to go one better than Fitzgerald and hold three somewhat contradictory ideas about the interrelationship between markets and government in your mind at the same time.
p132.zh: 美国作者F写道, “第一流思想的真正考验是同时持有两个相互矛盾的思想的能力”。斯科特·菲茨杰拉德(1896–1940). 在你研究微观经济学的时候,你应该能够比菲茨杰拉德做得更好,同时在思想中持有关于市场和政府相互关系的三种有些矛盾的想法.

p133.original: First, markets are extraordinarily useful and flexible institutions through which society can allocate its scarce resources. We introduced this idea with the subjects of international trade and demand and supply in other chapters and reinforced it in all the subsequent discussions of how households and firms make decisions.
p133.zh: 首先,市场是极为有用和灵活的机构,社会可以通过这些机构分配其稀缺的资源。 我们在其他章节中介绍了这一想法,并在随后关于家庭和公司如何作出决定的所有讨论中强化了这一想法。

p134.original: Second, markets may sometimes produce unwanted results. A short list of the cases in which markets produce unwanted results includes monopoly and other cases of imperfect competition, pollution, poverty and inequality of incomes, discrimination, and failure to provide insurance.
p134.zh: 第二,市场有时可能产生不想要的结果。市场产生意外结果的简略案例包括垄断和其他竞争不完善、污染、贫穷和收入不平等、歧视以及未能提供保险的案例。

p135.original: Third, while government may play a useful role in addressing the problems of markets, government action is also imperfect and may not reflect majority views. Economists readily admit that, in settings like monopoly or negative externalities, a potential role exists for government intervention. However, in the real world, it is not enough to point out that government action might be a good idea. Instead, we must have some confidence that the government is likely to identify and carry out the appropriate public policy. To make sensible judgments about economic policy, we must see the strengths and weaknesses of both markets and government. We must not idealize or demonize either unregulated markets or government actions. Instead, consider the actual strengths and weaknesses of real-world markets and real-world governments.
p135.zh: 第三,虽然政府在解决市场问题方面可能发挥有益的作用,但政府的行动也是不完善的,可能不能反映多数人的观点。经济学家们很容易地承认,在垄断或负面外部影响等环境中,政府干预可能发挥作用。 然而,在现实世界中,仅仅指出政府的行动可能是一个好主意是不够的。 相反,我们必须在一定程度上相信政府有可能确定并执行适当的公共政策。 为了对经济政策作出明智的判断,我们必须看到市场和政府的优势和弱点。 我们决不能理想化或妖魔化不受管制的市场或政府行动。 相反,考虑现实世界市场和现实世界政府的实际优势和弱点。

p136.original: These three insights seldom lead to simple or obvious political conclusions. As the famous British economist Joan Robinson wrote some decades ago: “[E]conomic theory, in itself, preaches no doctrines and cannot establish any universally valid laws. It is a method of ordering ideas and formulating questions.” The study of economics is neither politically conservative, nor moderate, nor liberal. There are economists who are Democrats, Republicans, libertarians, socialists, and members of every other political group you can name. Of course, conservatives may tend to emphasize the virtues of markets and the limitations of government, while liberals may tend to emphasize the shortcomings of markets and the need for government programs. Such differences only illustrate that the language and terminology of economics is not limited to one set of political beliefs, but can be used by all.
p136.zh: 这三个见解很少导致简单或明显的政治结论。 正如英国著名经济学家琼·鲁滨逊几十年前所写的那样:“经济学理论本身不宣扬任何理论,不能确立任何普遍适用的法律。经济学的研究既不是政治保守的,也不是温和的,也不是自由的。 有经济学家是民主党人,共和党人,自由主义者,社会主义者,还有可以指名的所有其他政治团体的成员. 当然,保守派可能倾向于强调市场的美德和政府的局限性,而自由派则可能倾向于强调市场的缺点和政府方案的必要性. 这种差异仅仅说明经济学的语言和术语并不限于一套政治信仰,而是可以被所有人使用.

p138.original: In April 2009, the union representing U.S. tire manufacturing workers filed a request with the U.S. International Trade Commission (ITC), asking it to investigate tire imports from China. Under U.S. trade law, if imports from a country increase to the point that they cause market disruption in the United States, as determined by the ITC, then it can also recommend a remedy for this market disruption. In this case, the ITC determined that from 2004 to 2008, U.S. tire manufacturers suffered declines in production, financial health, and employment as a direct result of increases in tire imports from China. The ITC recommended placing an additional tax on tire imports from China. President Obama and Congress agreed with the ITC recommendation, and in June 2009 tariffs on Chinese tires increased from 4% to 39%. In addition, tariffs on Chinese tires increased further as part of President Trump’s increases on a broad range of Chinese products.
p138.zh: 2009年4月,代表美国轮胎制造工人的工会向美国提出申请.国际贸易委员会(ITC),要求其调查轮胎从中国进口的情况. 根据美国贸易法,如果从一个国家进口的商品增加到由国贸中心确定的在美国造成市场混乱的程度,那么它也可以建议对这种市场混乱的补救办法。 在这种情况下,国贸中心确定,2004年至2008年,美国轮胎制造商的生产、财务健康和就业下降,这是从中国进口轮胎增加的直接结果。国贸中心建议对从中国进口的轮胎征收额外税。奥巴马总统和国会同意ITC的建议,2009年6月,中国轮胎的关税从4%提高到39%. 此外,由于川普总统对中国广泛产品加价的一部分,中国轮胎的关税进一步增加.

p139.original: Why would U.S. consumers buy imported tires from China in the first place? Most likely, because they are cheaper than tires produced domestically or in other countries. Therefore, this tariff increase should cause U.S. consumers to pay higher prices for tires, either because Chinese tires are now more expensive, or because U.S. consumers are pushed by the tariff to buy more expensive tires made by U.S. manufacturers or those from other countries. In the end, this tariff made U.S. consumers pay more for tires.
p139.zh: 美国消费者为何一开始就从中国购买进口轮胎?.很可能,因为这些轮胎比国内或其他国家生产的轮胎便宜。 因此,这种加税的做法应该促使美国消费者支付更高的轮胎价格,要么是因为中国轮胎现在更昂贵,要么是因为美国消费者被加税推向购买美国制造商或其他国家制造的更昂贵轮胎.最终,这种关税使得美国消费者为轮胎付出更多的费用.

p140.original: Was this tariff met with outrage expressed via social media, traditional media, or mass protests? Were there “Occupy Wall Street-type” demonstrations? The answer is a resounding “No”. Most U.S. tire consumers were likely unaware of the tariff increase, although they may have noticed the price increase, which was between $4 and $13 depending on the type of tire. Tire consumers are also potential voters. Conceivably, a tax increase, even a small one, might make voters unhappy. However, voters probably realized that it was not worth their time to learn anything about this issue or cast a vote based on it. They probably thought their vote would not matter in determining the outcome of an election or changing this policy.
p140.zh: 是否通过社交媒体、传统媒体或群众抗议,是否有“Occupy Wall Street型”示威游行?答案是响亮的“不”。 美国轮胎消费者大多可能不知道关税上涨,尽管他们可能注意到了价格上涨,根据轮胎的类型,涨价在4美元到13美元之间.轮胎消费者也是潜在的选民。 可以想象,增加税收,即使是小税收,也可能使选民不高兴。 然而,选民们可能意识到,他们不值得花时间了解这一问题或据此投票。 他们可能认为,在确定选举结果或改变这一政策时,他们的投票是无关紧要的。

p141.original: Estimates of the impact of this tariff show it costs U.S. consumers around $1.11 billion annually. Of this amount, roughly $817 million ends up in the pockets of foreign tire manufacturers other than in China, and the remaining $294 million goes to U.S. tire manufacturers. In other words, the tariff increase on Chinese tires may have saved 1,200 jobs in the domestic tire sector, but it cost 3,700 jobs in other sectors, as consumers had to reduce their spending because they were paying more for tires. People actually lost their jobs as a result of this tariff. Workers in U.S. tire manufacturing firms earned about $40,000 in 2010. Given the number of jobs saved and the total cost to U.S. consumers, the cost of saving one job amounted to $926,500!
p141.zh: 估计这种关税的影响表明,每年美国消费者花费约11.1亿美元。 其中,约8.17亿美元最终流入中国以外的外国轮胎制造商的口袋,其余2.94亿美元投向美国轮胎制造商.换句话说,中国轮胎的关税上涨可能节省了1,200个家庭轮胎部门的工作,但其他部门却花费了3,700个工作,因为消费者不得不削减开支,因为他们为轮胎支付更多的费用. 人们实际上因为这种关税而失去了工作.2010年美国轮胎制造企业的工人收入约为4万美元. 鉴于节省的工作数量和美国消费者的总成本,节省一份工作的成本达926,500美元!

p142.original: This tariff caused a net decline in U.S. social surplus. (We discuss total surplus in the Demand and Supply chapter, and tariffs in the Introduction to International Trade chapter.) Instead of saving jobs, it cost jobs, and those jobs that it saved cost many times more than the people working in them could ever hope to earn. Why would the government do this?
p142.zh: 这种关税导致美国社会盈余的净下降.(我们在“需求和供应”一章中讨论了总盈余,在“国际贸易导言”一章中讨论了关税。 )它不是节省工作,而是花费工作,而节省的工作比在他们中工作的人所希望的多得多。 政府为什么要这么做?

p143.original: The chapter answers this question by discussing the influence special interest groups have on economic policy. The steelworkers union, whose members make tires, saw increasingly more members lose their jobs as U.S. consumers consumed increasingly more cheap Chinese tires. By definition, this union is relatively small but well organized, especially compared to tire consumers. It stands to gain much for each of its members, compared to what each tire consumer may have to give up in terms of higher prices. Thus, the steelworkers union (joined by domestic tire manufacturers) has not only the means but the incentive to lobby economic policymakers and lawmakers. Given that U.S. tire consumers are a large and unorganized group, if they even are a group, it is unlikely they will lobby against higher tire tariffs. In the end, lawmakers tend to listen to those who lobby them, even though the results make for bad economic policy.
p143.zh: 本章通过讨论特殊利益集团对经济政策的影响来回答这个问题。钢铁工人工会的成员制造轮胎,随着美国消费者消费越来越便宜的中国轮胎,会员失业人数越来越多.顾名思义,这种结合虽然相对较小,但组织良好,尤其是与轮胎消费者相比.相对于每个轮胎消费者可能不得不以更高的价格放弃的东西而言,它为每个成员带来很多好处。 因此,钢铁工人工会(由国内轮胎制造商组成)不仅拥有游说经济决策者和立法者的手段,而且还有动力。 鉴于美国轮胎消费者是一个庞大且无组织的团体,如果他们甚至是一个团体,他们不太可能游说反对更高的轮胎关税.最终,立法者往往听从游说者的意见,尽管结果导致了糟糕的经济政策.

p145.original: Majority votes can run into difficulties when more than two choices exist. A voting cycle occurs when, in a situation with at least three choices, choice A is preferred by a majority vote to choice B, choice B is preferred by a majority vote to choice C, and choice C is preferred by a majority vote to choice A. In such a situation, it is impossible to identify what the majority prefers. Another difficulty arises when the vote is so divided that no choice receives a majority.
p145.zh: 如果存在两个以上的选择,多数选票可能会遇到困难。 在至少有三种选择的情况下,选择A以多数表决胜于选择B,选择B以多数表决胜于选择C,选择C以多数表决胜于选择A。 在这种情况下,不可能确定多数人喜欢什么。 当表决结果如此分裂以致没有选择获得多数时,又会出现另一个困难。

p146.original: A practical approach to microeconomic policy will need to take a realistic view of the specific strengths and weaknesses of markets as well as government, rather than making the easy but wrong assumption that either the market or government is always beneficial or always harmful.
p146.zh: 对微观经济政策采取实际做法,需要从现实的角度看待市场和政府的具体强项和弱点,而不是作出简单而错误的假设,即市场或政府总是有利或总是有害的。

p148.original: True or false: Majority rule can fail to produce a single preferred outcome when there are more than two choices.
p148.zh: 真假:在有两种以上选择的情况下,多数规则可能无法产生单一的首选结果。

p149.original: True. This is exactly what occurs in a voting cycle. That is, the majority can prefer policy A to policy B, policy B to policy C, but also prefer policy C to policy A. Then, the majority will never reach a conclusive outcome.
p149.zh: 没错。这正是在投票周期中发生的情况。也就是说,大多数人可以选择政策A而不是政策B,政策B而不是政策C,但也倾向于政策C而不是政策A. 那么,多数人将永远无法取得最终结果。

p151.original: The problem is an example of a voting cycle. The group will vote for mountain biking over canoeing by 2–1. It will vote for canoeing over the beach by 2–1. If mountain biking is preferred to canoeing and canoeing is preferred to the beach, it might seem that it must be true that mountain biking is the favorite. But in a vote of the beach versus mountain biking, the beach wins by a 2–1 vote. When a voting cycle occurs, choosing a single favorite that is always preferred by a majority becomes impossible.
p151.zh: 这个问题是一个投票周期的例子。 该组将投票支持山地自行车在2比1击沉舟山. 它将在2比1投票支持独木舟渡过海滩. 如果山地自行车更喜欢独木舟,而独木舟更喜欢海滩,那么,山地自行车是人们最喜爱的,这似乎一定是事实. 但海滩对山地自行车的投票中,海滩以2–1票胜出. 当一个投票周期出现时,选择一个总是为多数所偏爱的单一最爱就变得不可能了.

p152.original: Suppose there is an election for Soft Drink Commissioner. The field consists of one candidate from the Pepsi party and four from the Coca-Cola party. This would seem to indicate a strong preference for Coca-Cola among the voting population, but the Pepsi candidate ends up winning in a landslide. Why does this happen?
p152.zh: 如果有选举 软饮料专员。球场由百事党一名候选人和可口可乐党四名候选人组成. 这似乎表明投票人口中强烈倾向于可口可乐,但百事可乐候选人最终在一次滑坡中获胜.为什么会这样?

p153.original: The four Coca-Cola candidates compete with each other for Coca-Cola voters, whereas everyone who prefers Pepsi had only one candidate to vote for. Thus the will of the majority is not satisfied.
p153.zh: 4名可口可乐候选人相互竞争可口可乐选民,而所有喜欢百事可乐的人只有1名候选人投票. 因此,多数人的意愿没有得到满足。
